note: Three hand-authored personas for the AQ-10 autism screening engine. calculateAQ10 sums the ten pre-scored 0/1 fields q1..q10 (null = unanswered, skipped; rawResponses is display-only and ignored by both grader and detector), returns aq10Score, aq10CategoryLabel ('Below threshold' for <= 5, else 'At or above threshold') and firedRules = one row per item scoring 1, in item order. Flags are SPLIT: form-app.js calls detectAdditionalFlags(state) with the state alone, mirrored as flagsArgs ['state']; the oracle stores them under expected.additionalFlags. The detector recomputes the total itself (nulls as 0) and fires FLAG-AQ10-HIGH-001 at >= 6. Quirks verified in source: the two sensory flags are mutually exclusive (>= 2 severe -> -001 high, exactly 1 -> -002 medium); FLAG-REPETITIVE-002 and -003 both fire when resistanceToChange is 'always' and routineAdherence is 'always'; the developmental flags are naive case-insensitive substring tests for 'delay' or 'late', so an explicit negative ('No delay') and an unrelated word containing 'late' ('related') both fire them; the domain labels in aq10-rules.js do not match the published AQ-10 item domains (item 1 'notice small sounds' is labelled 'Social skills', item 7 'characters' intentions' is labelled 'Attention to detail'); the priority sort is stable so within a priority the flags keep detection order. Regenerate expected with: bin/test-personas autism-assessment --update

personas.name: Adult self-referral - AQ-10 2, no concerns
personas.description: A 34-year-old woman self-referring after reading about autism online; only two AQ-10 items score (item 1 noticing small sounds, item 8 collecting information), all social-communication ratings 'often', sensory profile none/mild, no repetitive movements, 'sometimes' resistance to change, typical milestones with no trigger words, no family history and no previous assessment. Expect aq10Score 2, aq10CategoryLabel 'Below threshold', firedRules [AQ10-01, AQ10-08] and an empty additionalFlags array.

personas.name: Adolescent at cut-off boundary - AQ-10 5, one item unanswered
personas.description: A 15-year-old boy referred by school; nine of ten AQ-10 items answered (item 3 skipped) scoring exactly 5, the top of 'Below threshold', so FLAG-AQ10-HIGH-001 does not fire. Exercises the engine's text quirks: languageMilestones is an explicit negative 'No delay...' which still fires FLAG-DEV-001 on the substring 'delay', and motorMilestones contains 'related' which fires FLAG-DEV-002 on the substring 'late'. Exactly one severe sensory modality (auditory) fires FLAG-SENSORY-002 (medium) rather than -001. Maternal depression gives the low-priority FLAG-FAMILY-MH-001. Expect aq10Score 5, 'Below threshold', firedRules [AQ10-01, AQ10-04, AQ10-07, AQ10-08, AQ10-10], and four flags in order: FLAG-SENSORY-002, FLAG-DEV-001, FLAG-DEV-002 (medium), FLAG-FAMILY-MH-001 (low).

personas.name: Child with maximal AQ-10 and every flag - urgent referral
personas.description: A 7-year-old boy referred by his GP with parent-completed AQ-10 scoring 10/10, severe sensitivity in all five modalities, eye contact 'never', reciprocity 'rarely', conversation 'never', hand-flapping, routine adherence and resistance to change both 'always', delayed language and late walking, positive family history for autism, ADHD, learning disability and mental health, and a previous incomplete assessment. Expect aq10Score 10, 'At or above threshold', firedRules all ten AQ10-01..AQ10-10 in order, and 15 flags: high = FLAG-AQ10-HIGH-001, FLAG-SENSORY-001 (5 severe), FLAG-REPETITIVE-003, FLAG-FAMILY-ASD-001; medium = FLAG-SOCIAL-001, -002, -003, FLAG-REPETITIVE-001, -002, FLAG-DEV-001, FLAG-DEV-002, FLAG-FAMILY-ADHD-001, FLAG-PREV-001; low = FLAG-FAMILY-LD-001, FLAG-FAMILY-MH-001.

firedRules.description: I often notice small sounds when others do not.
I usually concentrate more on the whole picture, rather than the small details.
I find it easy to do more than one thing at once.
If there is an interruption, I can switch back to what I was doing very quickly.
I find it easy to "read between the lines" when someone is talking to me.
I know how to tell if someone listening to me is getting bored.
When I am reading a story, I find it difficult to work out the characters' intentions.
I like to collect information about categories of things (e.g., types of car, bird, train, plant).
I find it easy to work out what someone is thinking or feeling just by looking at their face.
I find it difficult to work out people's intentions.
